item.text:
**It’s reasonable to raise the all-male panel as a concern about the selection process—but it isn’t, by itself, evidence that you were discriminated against.** It can raise questions about how the consultancy guards against bias, particularly when selecting leaders, without establishing why this decision was made.

Your qualifications and experience make your questions understandable. Still, the announcement isn’t a complete account of the successful candidate’s credentials or interview performance. For a group-head role, client relationships, business development and people management could legitimately carry substantial weight. The important question is **whether those criteria were relevant, established in advance and applied consistently**, rather than used after the fact to justify a preference.

I’d follow up in writing now, asking for:
- The selection criteria and their relative weighting.
- Feedback on your assessment against those criteria and the main reasons you were not selected.
- How the panel was constituted and what measures were used to ensure a fair, unbiased assessment.

You could write:

> I’m following up on my request of [date] for feedback on the appointment. I would appreciate an explanation of the selection criteria, their weighting and how my application was assessed, including the weight given to technical experience, leadership and client relationships. I also noticed that the panel consisted entirely of men. Could you explain how panel composition and safeguards against bias were considered?

The unanswered request is frustrating, but two weeks’ silence doesn’t itself establish bias. More significant warning signs would include shifting explanations, departures from published criteria, sex-related comments or different standards being applied to candidates.

**Keep the advertisement, correspondence and your interview notes.** If you’re considering a formal complaint, seek local employment-equality advice promptly; time limits can be short, and waiting for feedback may not pause them.

Which country was the job in? That determines whether you have a right to a written explanation and what rules, if any, apply to panel composition.
